claims.claim: Origen of Alexandria was an early Christian theologian and ascetic who lived from approximately 185 to 253 CE.
Origen was born at Alexandria of Christian parents and was educated in the Catechetical School of Alexandria under Pantaenus and Clement.
Origen became head of the Catechetical School of Alexandria, first informally and then officially in 203.
On the First Principles (Peri Archon/De Principiis) was the first systematic exposition of Christian theology.
On the First Principles is thought to have been written around 220–230 AD, when Origen was around forty-five years of age.

Origen wrote On the First Principles to provide a unified discussion of Christian teachings so that readers could probe more deeply into the church's rule of faith and discriminate among conflicting scriptural interpretations in Alexandria in the late 220s.
The work was addressed to a reader named Macarius, as indicated in Rufinus's preface to Book III.
The full Greek text of On the First Principles has not been completely preserved.
Fragments from Books 3.1 and 4.1-3 of Origen's Greek original are preserved in Origen's Philocalia.
A few smaller quotations of the original Greek are preserved in Justinian's Letter to Mennas.
The vast majority of the text has survived in a Latin translation produced by Tyrannius Rufinus in 397.
